title: KO-04-C3 Retention under read pressure

events.label: setup: v1 = A, retention KEEP_VERSIONS=3
events.detail: Version n holds 64 copies of the n-th letter. GC keeps only the newest 3 versions.

events.label: read CURRENT -> v1
events.detail: Lock-free read: the pointer says the committed version is v1.

events.label: reader PAUSED after reading CURRENT -> v1
events.detail: The reader thread is descheduled between reading the pointer and opening v000001.dat (read_hook blocks on a threading.Event). Readers take no lock.

events.label: append BEGIN record -> journal.wal
events.detail: Write-ahead intent: the BEGIN record (old -> new version, SHA-256 of the new body, salted CRC) is appended to the journal BEFORE any data is written, so recovery can recognise this save if we die mid-way.

events.label: fsync journal.wal
events.detail: fsync makes the BEGIN record durable: from now on recovery will know this save was in flight.

events.label: create .v000002.dat.tmp
events.detail: Copy-on-write: v2 goes into a brand-new temp file created with O_CREAT|O_EXCL in the same directory. The current version is never modified in place.

events.label: write 132 B -> .v000002.dat.tmp
events.detail: The version frame (header + SHA-256 + body) is written. It sits only in the kernel page cache until fsync: dataDurable=false, a power cut could lose or tear it.

events.label: fsync .v000002.dat.tmp
events.detail: fsync BEFORE rename: the data must be on stable storage before any name points at it (the ext4 zero-length-file lesson, 2009). dataDurable turns true.

events.label: rename .v000002.dat.tmp -> v000002.dat
events.detail: rename(2) atomically gives the finished file its final name v000002.dat. It is NOT current: CURRENT still names the old version, so readers and recovery ignore it.

events.label: fsync dir report
events.detail: fsync(dir) makes the new name v000002.dat durable (PostgreSQL durable_rename lesson). The version is safely on disk but is NOT the current version yet.

events.label: create .CURRENT.tmp
events.detail: The new one-line pointer is prepared in its own temp file (O_CREAT|O_EXCL), never by editing CURRENT in place.

events.label: write 91 B -> .CURRENT.tmp
events.detail: Pointer text 'ADOC-CURRENT <format> <version> <sha256> <crc32>': self-validating, so a torn pointer can never be mistaken for a good one. Not durable yet.

events.label: fsync .CURRENT.tmp
events.detail: The pointer bytes are flushed BEFORE the rename that will publish them.

events.label: rename .CURRENT.tmp -> CURRENT
events.detail: COMMIT POINT. rename() atomically replaces CURRENT: before this instruction every reader and every recovery sees the old version, after it the new one. There is no state in between. (Durable only after the directory fsync that follows.)

events.label: fsync dir report
events.detail: DURABLE COMMIT: flushing the directory makes the CURRENT swap survive power loss. Only now does put() return success to the caller.

events.label: append COMMIT record -> journal.wal
events.detail: Completion record. The save is already committed by the CURRENT rename; COMMIT only tells recovery that this transaction finished cleanly.

events.label: fsync journal.wal
events.detail: fsync makes the COMMIT record durable.

events.label: retention: never more than 3 version files after a save
v1 was garbage-collected when v4 committed
reader stayed paused during all 5 saves
reader resumes
events.detail: It now opens v000001.dat - which GC deleted.

events.label: read v000001.dat -> ENOENT
events.detail: The version named by CURRENT a moment ago is gone: a writer committed newer versions and garbage collection deleted it. The reader must re-read CURRENT.

events.label: read CURRENT -> v6
events.detail: Lock-free read: the pointer says the committed version is v6.

events.label: retry 1: CURRENT now names v6
events.detail: A FileNotFoundError proves a newer version committed, so re-reading CURRENT is safe.

events.label: read v000006.dat (SHA-256 ok)
events.detail: Header and SHA-256 verify: v000006.dat is a whole version.

events.label: get() returned v6 = F after 2 attempts
events.detail: A whole committed version, verified by SHA-256 - never a mix, never an error.

events.label: reader returned v6 exactly (no error, no mix)
the bound: reader starved on EVERY attempt
events.detail: Each time the reader pauses, writers commit 3 versions, so the version it just read is always GC'd before it can open it.

events.label: ReadContention after 5 attempts
events.detail: Instead of looping forever or blocking writers, get() gives up after READ_RETRIES=5 attempts with a clear error. 'report': version removed by GC 5 times in a row
